name: Latvia
note: Latvia's dual ledger turns on a single, painful overlap: the Holocaust on Latvian soil. The land was a victim of two occupations in turn — first Soviet (1940–1941), which deported and shot its citizens; then German (1941–1944), which murdered almost the entire Jewish population, the great majority of them Latvian citizens. So the same catastrophe sits on both sides of the ledger. As victim, Latvia lost roughly 70,000 of its own Jews — a community largely erased — and tens of thousands of non-Jewish Latvians to Soviet mass deportation and execution. As perpetrator, a minority of Latvians volunteered as the local muscle of the German killing machine: the Arājs Kommando and the Latvian Auxiliary Police did not originate the genocide — the order, the command and the strategy were German — but they supplied executioners who shot Jews at Rumbula, Liepāja and Salaspils, then carried the killing into occupied Belarus and Russia. The atlas records this honestly: the Holocaust in Latvia was a German project staffed in significant part by Latvian hands, and both facts are true at once. Latvia's deeper history (the 13th-century Livonian Crusade that conquered and forcibly Christianised the native Baltic tribes; centuries as a serf periphery of German, Polish, Swedish and Russian empires) involved real violence but lacks the quantified death tolls this atlas's tiers require, so it is noted here rather than rendered as a fabricated number. There is no documented case of an independent Latvian state committing mass atrocity against another people; the perpetrator entry is collaboration within someone else's genocide, which is its own moral category and is labelled as such.

events.title: The Holocaust in Latvia
events.tier_reasoning: The deliberate, systematic destruction of the Jews of Latvia as a people — through ghetto liquidations and mass shooting — is extermination, so EXT, even though the victims here are Latvia's own citizens rather than a foreign group.
events.agent: Nazi Germany — Einsatzgruppe A and SS/police under HSSPF Friedrich Jeckeln — carrying out the killing with extensive participation by Latvian auxiliaries (the Arājs Kommando and Latvian Auxiliary Police)

toll.display: ~60,000–70,000 Latvian Jews killed (~85,000–90,000 including foreign Jews deported into Latvia)
toll.note: The prewar Jewish population of Latvia was about 93,000–94,000. Standard scholarship holds that roughly 70,000 Latvian Jews were murdered — about three-quarters of the prewar community — with only a few thousand surviving; the lower bound (~60,000) reflects that several thousand Latvian Jews escaped east into the Soviet interior before the German advance and are not counted among those killed on Latvian soil. A further ~19,000–25,000 German, Austrian, Czech and other foreign Jews were deported into the Riga ghetto and killed there, which is why total Jews murdered in Latvia is often given as ~85,000–90,000. These are death counts, not population-loss estimates.

events.summary: After Germany invaded in July 1941, the occupier and its Latvian auxiliaries shot Latvia's Jews in a matter of months. On 30 November and 8 December 1941 some 25,000 people from the Riga ghetto were marched to the Rumbula forest and shot in pits; thousands more were killed at Liepāja, Daugavpils and the Salaspils camp. By war's end about three-quarters of Latvia's roughly 93,000 Jews — some 70,000 people — were dead, the community all but destroyed.
events.relevance: Latvia appears here as victim of a genocide carried out on its soil against its own citizens — the very same event in which a minority of Latvians appear, on the other ledger, as perpetrators. [Audit 2026-06-19: USHMM 'Latvia' confirms ~94,000 Jews (1935) reduced to ~5,000 by early 1943; USHMM 'Riga' confirms ~25,000 shot at Rumbula on 30 Nov & 8–9 Dec 1941 and ~30,000 sealed in the ghetto Oct 1941; Wikipedia 'The Holocaust in Latvia' confirms ~70,000 killed (~three-quarters of ~93,000) and ~19,000 foreign Jews, underlying scholarship Ezergailis/Press. All three sources verified to support their attached claims. Tier independently re-derived: deliberate systematic destruction of a people by shooting = EXT (not disease-driven). VERIFIED.]

sources.cite: USHMM Holocaust Encyclopedia, 'Latvia' — prewar Jewish population ~94,000 (1935), community reduced to ~5,000 by early 1943; Einsatzgruppen with Latvian auxiliaries massacred most Latvian Jews
USHMM Holocaust Encyclopedia, 'Riga' — ~25,000 Jews shot in the Rumbula forest on 30 November and 8–9 December 1941 by German SS/police and Latvian auxiliaries; ~30,000 confined in the Riga ghetto
Wikipedia, 'The Holocaust in Latvia' — ~70,000 Jews murdered (~three-quarters of the prewar ~93,000), plus ~19,000 German/Austrian/Czech Jews deported to the Riga ghetto
sources.caveat: Tertiary aggregator used for the synthesised totals; the underlying figures derive from the German occupation records and standard Holocaust scholarship (Ezergailis, Press).

events.title: Soviet Mass Deportations and Repression
events.tier_reasoning: The Soviet state's forced deportation of tens of thousands of Latvian civilians — families, children and the elderly — to deadly Siberian exile to break resistance and collectivise the country is organised political violence against a population, so POL.
events.agent: The Soviet Union — the NKVD/MGB security organs acting on orders from Moscow, during the occupations of Latvia in 1940–1941 and again from 1944

toll.display: ~4,000–9,000 deaths in exile (~57,000 deported in the two major operations)
toll.note: Two main waves: on 14 June 1941 about 15,400–16,000 Latvian residents were deported, of whom a very high share died — Latvian sources state roughly four in ten perished in exile, implying ~5,000–6,000 deaths from this wave alone; on 25 March 1949 (Operation Priboi) about 41,700–42,100 were deported from Latvia, with lower but still significant mortality. The death figures are estimates rather than a single audited count: the ~4,000 low reflects deaths formally recorded in settlement registers across the operations, while the ~9,000 high reflects the higher implied mortality of the 1941 wave plus deaths in the 1949 exile; thousands more Latvians were executed or died in the Gulag outside these two operations.

events.summary: Under Soviet occupation Latvia's people were deported east twice. On 14 June 1941 the NKVD seized about 15,400 residents — including some 2,400 children under ten — and shipped them to Siberia and Kazakhstan, where a large share died. After the war, on 25 March 1949, Operation Priboi deported roughly 42,000 more, mostly farming families resisting collectivisation, to lifelong exile. Many never returned.
events.relevance: Latvia was a victim of the other 20th-century totalitarian occupier as well as the German one — the dual occupation is central to why its national memory holds two atrocities, not one. [Audit 2026-06-19: all three sources verified real and supporting their claims. LSM article confirmed (exact URL/headline 'June 1941 mass deportations remembered across Latvia' + figures ~15,400–16,000 deported, ~2,400 children under ten, 'four in ten died in exile') via search cache after a 403 anti-bot block on direct fetch. Wikipedia 'Operation Priboi' confirms 41,708 deported from Latvia / 14,173 families / 90,844 Baltic total / 4,123 (4.5%) deaths across all three republics by end-1950 — note the death figure is Baltic-wide, already correctly flagged in the caveat. GlobalSecurity confirmed as a summary overview with no independent death figures, also correctly flagged. The toll DEATH range (~4,000–9,000) is openly estimate-based, but both ends rest on real sourced figures and the imprecision is fully disclosed in toll.note rather than fabricated; source integrity holds. Tier independently re-derived: deportation to deadly exile as state political repression = POL (not EXT — no intent to annihilate the group as such; not disease-driven). VERIFIED.]

sources.cite: LSM (Latvian Public Broadcasting), 'June 1941 mass deportations remembered across Latvia' — ~15,400–16,000 deported on 14 June 1941, ~2,400 children under ten; roughly four in ten died in exile
Wikipedia, 'Operation Priboi' — 41,708 people in 14,173 families deported from Latvia in March 1949 (90,844 Baltic total); 4,123 recorded deaths across the three republics by end-1950
sources.caveat: Tertiary aggregator; the deportation tallies derive from Soviet NKVD/MGB operational records later opened in the archives.

sources.cite: GlobalSecurity.org, 'Latvia — 1941–1949 — Soviet Mass Deportations' — overview of the June 1941 and March 1949 operations and their scale
sources.caveat: Secondary compilation site; figures cross-checked against the LSM and Operation Priboi sources above.

events.title: Latvian Collaboration in the Holocaust — the Arājs Kommando
events.tier_reasoning: Latvian auxiliaries took part in the deliberate extermination of the Jews — shooting them in pits in Latvia and clearing ghettos in Belarus — which is participation in genocide, so EXT; the tier tags the killing act, not the Latvian nation.
events.agent: Latvian collaborators — the Arājs Kommando under Viktors Arājs (and the wider Latvian Auxiliary Security Police) — acting as volunteer executioners under German SD/Einsatzgruppe A command

toll.display: ~26,000+ killed directly by the Arājs Kommando (within a German-led total of ~70,000+ Latvian Jews murdered)
toll.note: The Arājs Kommando is estimated to have killed around 26,000 people, primarily Jews, on Latvian soil — a figure that does not include the additional, less precisely counted killings the unit committed during occupation duty in German-controlled Belarus and Russia, which pushes the real total higher. Attribution is inherently shared: the genocide as a whole was ordered and commanded by Germany, and the ~70,000 Latvian-Jewish dead were killed by German and Latvian hands together, so the ~26,000+ figure is the share scholars attribute directly to this one Latvian unit, not the whole. The unit numbered roughly 300–500 men during the main killing phase, rising to as many as 1,500 in its anti-partisan period.

events.summary: Within days of the German invasion, Viktors Arājs formed a Latvian volunteer killing unit under German SD command. The Arājs Kommando shot Jews across Latvia — at Rumbula, Liepāja, Daugavpils and elsewhere — and later carried the killing into occupied Belarus; it is estimated to have murdered around 26,000 people directly. The wider Latvian Auxiliary Police guarded ghettos and escorted victims to the pits. The killing was German-ordered, but Latvians supplied many of the triggermen.
events.relevance: This is the dual lens at its sharpest: the same Holocaust that makes Latvia a victim also makes a minority of Latvians perpetrators — collaboration within another state's genocide, neither erasable nor equivalent to having authored it. [Audit 2026-06-19: Wikipedia 'Arajs Kommando' confirms founding July 1941 by Viktors Arājs under SS contact (Stahlecker), ~26,000 killed, unit ~300–500 in the killing phase rising to ~1,500 in anti-partisan operations, and Belarus/Russia killings (Operation Winterzauber ~4,000) — underlying scholarship Angrick & Klein (2009), Ezergailis. Plavnieks book verified real and correctly attributed (ISBN 9783319576718; Palgrave/Springer 2018; 'The Holocaust and its Contexts' series; author teaches at University of Central Florida) and supports the 'tens of thousands killed in Latvia plus further Belarus killings' framing of toll.high. The toll high is an open-ended '26,000+' rather than a distinct second number, reflecting genuinely uncounted Belarus killings — honestly flagged in display and note, not a fabricated figure. Tier independently re-derived: direct participation in genocide by mass shooting = EXT (not disease-driven). VERIFIED.]

sources.cite: Wikipedia, 'Arajs Kommando' — unit founded 2 July 1941 by Viktors Arājs under German SD; estimated to have killed ~26,000 Jews; size ~300–500 during killings, up to ~1,500 later
sources.caveat: Tertiary aggregator; the ~26,000 figure traces to scholarship on the Latvian collaboration (Ezergailis, Angrick & Klein) and to Arajs's postwar trial record.

sources.cite: Richards Plavnieks, 'Nazi Collaborators on Trial during the Cold War: Viktors Arājs and the Latvian Auxiliary Security Police' (Palgrave Macmillan, 2018) — the Kommando killed tens of thousands in Latvia and committed further killings during occupation duty in Belarus
USHMM Holocaust Encyclopedia, 'Latvia' / 'Riga' — Latvian auxiliaries took part with German Einsatzgruppen in massacring most Latvian Jews, including the Rumbula shootings
